The test image shows a **tomato leaf** with:
- Large brown/tan necrotic area covering most of the upper and right portions
- Yellow chlorotic border transitioning from green tissue to brown necrosis
- Small dark spots scattered across the leaf surface
- No powdery coating, no gray fuzzy growth, no mosaic pattern

This is a **leaf** image. Leaf-indexed candidates: Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato, Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus, Early_Blight, Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Leaf_Mold, Powdery_Mildew, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Verticillium_Wilt.

The large marginal necrosis with yellow halo is most consistent with Verticillium_Wilt or Late_Blight. Let me check references starting with Verticillium_Wilt.
Verticillium Wilt reference shows wilting/yellowing without the distinct brown necrosis and dark spots I see in the test image. Not a strong match. Let me check Late_Blight.
That's a microscopic image (spores), not useful for macroscopic comparison. Let me check the other Late_Blight leaf reference.
Late Blight shows water-soaked dark/gray lesions - not matching the test image's tan-brown necrosis with yellow border. Let me check Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus.
TSWV shows bronzing with scattered small spots - the test image has a different pattern (large marginal necrosis). Let me check Early_Blight.
Early Blight shows distinct dark concentric ring lesions - the test image has a large marginal brown/tan necrotic area, not the concentrated concentric spots. Let me check Septoria_Leaf_Blotch.
Septoria shows small dark spots on yellowing leaf - somewhat similar to the test image with scattered dark spots. Let me check Gray_Mold.
Gray Mold shows brown marginal necrosis - somewhat similar pattern to test image, but test image has many more scattered dark spots. Let me check Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt.

Bacterial Canker shows brown marginal necrosis (scorching at leaf margins) - similar to test image. But the test image has a prominent yellow zone and many scattered small dark spots. Let me check Bacterial_Speck.
Bacterial Speck shows small dark spots on green leaf - the dark spots are similar to test image but test image has a much larger necrotic area. Let me check Leaf_Mold.
Leaf Mold shows yellow spots without the large necrotic lesion of the test image. Let me check Powdery_Mildew.
Powdery Mildew shows white powdery coating - not matching the test image at all. Let me check Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus.
CMV shows mosaic/malformed leaves - clearly not a match. Now I need to cover remaining classes. Let me check the non-leaf classes to fulfill the 16-class requirement.
Another microscopic spore image - not comparable to field symptoms. Let me check Anthracnose.
Anthracnose shows fruit pod with dark lesions - not a leaf image. Let me cover the last 2 uncovered classes.

Both Sclerotinia and Southern Blight are stem diseases - not relevant to the test leaf image.

**Summary of all 16 reference views across 15 distinct classes:**

| Class | Match to test image |
|---|---|
| Septoria_Leaf_Blotch | **Best match** - small dark spots (pycnidia) on yellowing/browning leaf |
| Early_Blight | Partial - dark lesions with yellow halos but distinct concentric rings not in test |
| Gray_Mold | Partial - brown marginal necrosis, but test has many more scattered spots |
| Bacterial_Canker | Partial - marginal browning, but test has pycnidia-like dark spots |
| Bacterial_Speck | Partial - small dark spots, but test has much larger necrotic area |
| Verticillium_Wilt | No - wilting/yellowing only |
| Late_Blight | No - water-soaked dark/gray lesions |
| TSWV | No - bronzing pattern |
| Powdery_Mildew | No - white powdery coating |
| Leaf_Mold | No - yellow spots only |
| CMV | No - mosaic/malformed |
| Alternaria/Southern_Blight/Sclerotinia/Anthracnose | No - stem/fruit diseases |

**Conclusion:** The test image shows tan-brown necrotic tissue with many small dark spots consistent with **pycnidia** (Septoria's diagnostic fruiting bodies), a yellow chlorotic transition zone, and coalescing lesions causing widespread leaf blight. This matches Septoria_Leaf_Blotch most closely.

The tan/gray necrotic color and pycnidia-like dark spots match Septoria_Leaf_Blotch more closely than Early_Blight (which has distinct concentric rings), Late_Blight (water-soaked dark lesions), or Bacterial_Canker (papery marginal scorch without pycnidia)."}
